title: [28/11/2020] CO2 emissions
prompt: The graph below shows average carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions per person in the United Kingdom, Sweden, Italy and Portugal between 1967 and 2007. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph compares four countries in terms of the amount of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions per person per tonnes, measured in tonnes, between 1967 and 2007.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: It is clear that the production of CO2 emissions in the United Kingdom and Portugal both declined while the opposite was the case for Italy and Sweden during the period shown. Additionally, out of four countries in the timeframe, the United Kingdom’s numbers were much higher in most of the years shown.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the United Kingdom and Portugal, in 1967 the UK's emissions stood at approximately 11 tons per person, which was about 3 tonnes higher than Portugal's figure of 8 tons. Subsequently, the production of individual emissions in the UK declined steadily to around 8 tons by 2007, while Portugal's number rose to nearly 10 tons in 1977 before falling dramatically to approximately 5.8 tons by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining countries, in 1967, the amount of CO2 emitted in Italy was 4 tons per capita, which was more than double Sweden's figure of less than 2 tons. Thereafter, both countries saw consistent increases over the forty-year period, with Italy reaching roughly 8 tons and Sweden climbing to about 5.5 tons in 2007.
